To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of timestamp values in the context of database transactions is a promising approach for capturing transaction time and valid time, that the commit time of a transaction is a useful timestamp value for the results of the transaction, and that the current time is an appropriate timestamp for facts that are valid until now.

the timestamping of bitemporal facts can be done in a variety of ways, and that these ways can be classified into three categories: (i) timestamping with the commit time, (ii) timestamping with an explicit substitute for now, and (iii) timestamping with a derived value.

(1) the timestamping of database facts in the context of a transaction is an important and difficult problem, (2) straightforward timestamping of facts is problematic, and (3) the proposed solutions provide efficient and effective support for the timestamping of bitemporal data in the context of transaction processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of timestamp-based temporal models for capturing transaction and/or valid time in the database context.

the use of timestamped values for representing the time of transaction and valid time, and with the use of timestamps in transactions for the purpose of maintaining the temporal properties of the database.
the effective use of timestamping in databases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of timestamps in the database context is an extremely complex and difficult problem.
the techniques presented in this paper are effective in solving most problems with straightforward timestamp assignment, but that there are a few cases where the techniques are not applicable.
the use of transaction and valid time is not a problem in database systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
timestamping in databases is not straightforward.
we have shown how to timestamp database data effectively, and how to modify this effectively timestamped data efficiently.

we propose and evaluate a number of techniques that allow application programmers to use bitemporal tables as if they were ordinary tables, while at the same time providing the database system with the necessary information to efficiently timestamp and maintain the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
effective timestamping requires careful consideration of the transaction context.
timestamping can be used for capturing transaction and, in particular, valid time in the database, provided that it is done with care.
timestamping in databases can be effective and efficient.
